title: Characters and animation style
purpose: Classifies the visual style family and, when characters or drawn elements appear, lifts their construction, frame rate, poses, lip sync and secondary motion.
boundary: The swarm lifts technique and structure only. Never store, transcribe or reuse the source's footage, frames, music, voice or script text. Keyframes and spectrograms are temporary analysis files in a scratch directory and are never copied into the format IR or a variant. On-screen text may be quoted only as a locating note in evidence.note, at most 6 words, and narration is never quoted. Patterns replace content words with slots, e.g. 'FACT {n}' or '{number} {unit} {noun}'. Analysing a public video for technique is fine; republishing its content is not.
inspect: F8 frame steps to count unique drawings per second; F3 crops for line weight and fill; F2 bursts for cycles.
pitfalls: Calling footage 'animation' because it is stylised
Measuring frame holds over a section where the camera also moves
Naming the tool used to make it as fact; it is inferred

methods.measured: A measurement tool produced the value (an evidence.json field or an ffmpeg/ffprobe filter output). Name the tool and the field.
methods.observed: You looked at extracted frames, crops, scopes, spectrograms or waveforms and saw it. Give the timestamps you looked at.
methods.inferred: Reasoned from measured or observed facts, e.g. 'synthetic voice' from flat pitch on a spectrogram. State the reasoning in the note.
methods.assumed: No direct evidence; a default or convention. Use only for gaps the format needs filled, and keep confidence at 0.3 or lower.

pointer_conventions: ir_path is a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the Video format IR (contract schema video_re_format_ir).
A final '/-' means 'append this answer to the array' (the RFC 6901 end-of-array token), e.g. /motion/transitions/- or /generation_rules/-.
A '*' segment means 'each array element the answer is about'; the answer must say which elements (for example beats with role 'item'). The lifter resolves '*' to concrete indexes.
Paths under free-form objects (typography.title, typography.captions, typography.labels, audio.narration, audio.music, render_binding.mapping) use the snake_case key named in the question.

answer_types.number: {"value": n, "unit": "..."} optionally with "min" and "max"; becomes an IR observed_number
answer_types.ms: {"value": n, "unit": "ms"} optionally with "min"/"max"; signed when an offset (negative = earlier)
answer_types.enum: exactly one of the question's choices (a string)
answer_types.list: array of short strings (technique names or kinds)
answer_types.object: a JSON object with the keys the question's how_to_answer names

recipes.F2: Burst sheet, 10 frames over 1 s: ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t 1 -i "$SRC" -vf "fps=10,scale=270:-2,tile=5x2" -frames:v 1 "$WORK/burst_T.jpg"
recipes.F3: Full-resolution crop (add ,scale=iw*2:-1:flags=lanczos to enlarge): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -i "$SRC" -frames:v 1 -vf "crop=W:H:X:Y" "$WORK/crop_T.png"
recipes.F4: Whole-video contact sheet, 1 frame per second: ffmpeg -v error -i "$SRC" -vf "fps=1,scale=180:-2,tile=8x8" -frames:v 1 "$WORK/sheet.jpg" (or use the keyframes and contact sheet from video_re_keyframes_contact_sheet)
recipes.F8: Every frame in a short window (animation timing; frame k is at T + k/fps): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t 0.5 -i "$SRC" -vf "scale=540:-2" "$WORK/step_T_%03d.png"
recipes.F9: Average colour of a region: ffmpeg -v error -ss T -i "$SRC" -frames:v 1 -vf "crop=W:H:X:Y,scale=1:1:flags=area,format=rgb24" -f rawvideo - | od -An -tu1
recipes.F10: Similarity of two frames (SSIM, 1.0 = identical): ffmpeg -i a.jpg -i b.jpg -lavfi "[0:v]scale=320:-2[a];[1:v]scale=320:-2[b];[a][b]ssim" -f null - 2>&1 | grep -o "All:[0-9.]*"
recipes.A1: Spectrogram image (add highpass=f=3000, before showspectrumpic to isolate clicks and whooshes): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t D -i "$SRC" -lavfi "showspectrumpic=s=1200x600:legend=1" "$WORK/spec_T.png"

questions.question: Which visual style family fits best (live-action, photo montage, 2D flat vector, stick figure, cut-out, layered 2.5D, low-poly 3D, textured 3D, pixel art, voxel, whiteboard or sketch, kinetic type, screen capture)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills visual.style_family, which picks the renderer.
questions.how_to_answer: Classify from the F4 contact sheet and 5 F1 frames; give the share of runtime per family if mixed.
questions.challenge: A stylised filter over footage is still live-action; check for photographic texture on F3 crops.

questions.question: Are there characters (people, animals, mascots, objects with faces), and how many distinct ones?
questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether the format needs character rigs.
questions.how_to_answer: Count distinct characters on the contact sheet; describe each by construction only (no identities).
questions.challenge: Do not count real people in photos as characters; they belong to shot_list_framing.

questions.question: How are characters constructed (stick lines, flat shapes, rigged cut-out parts, frame-by-frame drawings, 3D models)?
questions.how_to_answer: F3 crops at joints: hinged parts that rotate rigidly indicate cut-out rigs; redrawn shapes per frame indicate frame-by-frame.
questions.challenge: Check two different poses of the same character.

questions.question: At what rate do drawings or poses change (on ones, twos, threes, or held poses) relative to the video frame rate?
questions.how_to_answer: F8 steps over 0.5 s of character motion; count frames where the character changes; compare with fps.
questions.challenge: Camera moves change every frame regardless; measure on a section with a still camera.

questions.question: What line style is used (stroke weight in px, outline colour, clean or sketchy)?
questions.how_to_answer: F3 enlarged crops; measure stroke width at full resolution.

questions.question: How are shapes filled (flat colour, gradient, texture, cel-shaded with shadow bands)?
questions.how_to_answer: F3 crops of filled areas.
questions.challenge: Compression banding on gradients is not cel shading.

questions.question: What are character proportions (head height to body height ratio)?
questions.how_to_answer: Measure on F3 crops of a standing pose.
questions.challenge: Use a neutral standing pose; foreshortening skews it.

questions.question: How many facial expression states are used, and how are they drawn (none, dots and lines, full faces)?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets the expression set size for a rig.
questions.how_to_answer: Collect distinct face states on F3 crops across the video.

questions.question: Is there lip sync, and of what kind (none, open/close flap, viseme shapes)?
questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether a lip-sync tool (for example Rhubarb Lip Sync) is needed.
questions.how_to_answer: F8 on a speaking character; count distinct mouth shapes and compare with speech timing.
questions.challenge: Mouth movement without speech alignment is not lip sync.

questions.question: Do characters blink, and how often?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a blink rate to idle animation.
questions.how_to_answer: Count blinks over 10 s of on-screen character time using F2 bursts.

questions.question: Are walk or run cycles used, and how many frames is one cycle?
questions.how_to_answer: F8 over 1 s of walking; find the frame where the pose repeats.
questions.challenge: A sliding character with no leg motion has no cycle.

questions.question: Is there secondary motion (follow-through on hair, clothing, tails, props)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds secondary motion to the rig spec.
questions.how_to_answer: F8 after a character stops: parts that keep moving.

questions.question: Is squash and stretch used on characters or props?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds deformation to the animation style.
questions.how_to_answer: F8 on impacts and jumps; measure height/width changes.

questions.question: How do characters enter the scene (pop in, walk in, draw on, fade, already present)?
questions.how_to_answer: F8 at first appearances.

questions.question: Do props and environments share the characters' style (line weight, fill, palette)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a consistency rule for asset generation.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare F3 crops of props with characters.

questions.question: From which viewpoint is the scene shown (side view, top-down, isometric, front, three-quarter)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills the projection for 2D or 3D renderers.
questions.how_to_answer: Inspect floor lines and object faces on F1 frames.
questions.challenge: Isometric shows parallel receding lines at about 30 degrees; measure one.

questions.question: Do falling or bouncing objects follow plausible gravity (accelerating falls, decaying bounces)?
questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether a physics engine (for example Pymunk) is needed.
questions.how_to_answer: Track an object's height over F8 frames; check for increasing per-frame displacement while falling.

questions.question: How many distinct poses does each character use?
questions.how_to_answer: Group F3 crops of a character by pose.
questions.challenge: Mirrored poses count once; say how mirrors were treated.

questions.question: Does the background art match the character style or contrast with it (for example photo backgrounds behind drawn characters)?
questions.how_to_answer: Compare F3 crops.

questions.question: Do characters cast contact shadows on the ground?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds contact shadows to the scene recipe.
questions.how_to_answer: F3 crops at feet.

questions.question: Is the motion snappy (fast moves with holds) or floaty (continuous slow easing)?
questions.how_to_answer: From F8 series, compare move duration with hold duration.

questions.question: How long are holds between key poses (ms)?
questions.how_to_answer: F8 series: count frames where the pose does not change between moves.

questions.question: Are motion lines, smears or impact frames used?
questions.how_to_answer: F8 on fast actions.

questions.question: Is each character colour-coded (one dominant colour per character)?
questions.how_to_answer: F9 on each character's main area.

questions.question: For 2.5D scenes, how many depth planes are there and how do their parallax speeds compare?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills depth plane count and parallax ratios.
questions.how_to_answer: Track features on each plane between two frames of a move.
questions.challenge: Planes moving by animation (not camera) must be excluded.

questions.question: Which open-source tools could reproduce this style (for example Motion Canvas, Manim, Blender, Godot, Synfig, OpenToonz, Pymunk for physics)?
questions.why_it_matters: Gives the render binding a renderer hint; always inferred.
questions.how_to_answer: Map style features (vector vs 3D, rigging, physics) to tools known to support them; mark method inferred and do not claim the source used them.
questions.challenge: Any statement that the source was made with a named tool is rejected unless the video shows it.

questions.question: Which character and style parameters should a new video set (style family, rig asset, palette, line weight, fps)?
Do character actions follow the narration (a gesture or action when the key word is spoken)?
questions.how_to_answer: Compare action start times (F8) with word onsets (A1) for 4 actions.

questions.question: Is text integrated into the scene (signs, labels attached to objects, speech bubbles)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds diegetic text to the style.
questions.how_to_answer: Inspect F1 frames for text attached to objects.
questions.challenge: Captions placed near objects are not diegetic unless attached and moving with them.

questions.question: Does a character's appearance stay consistent between shots (same proportions, colours, features)?
questions.why_it_matters: Tells the pipeline it needs a fixed character sheet or reusable rig.
questions.how_to_answer: F10 and F3 comparisons of the same character in different shots.
questions.challenge: List the shots compared and any differences found.

questions.question: How many scenes (distinct environments) does each item use?
questions.how_to_answer: Group shots per item by environment.

questions.question: Before a comedic or dramatic impact, how long is the pause (ms) between set-up and impact?
questions.how_to_answer: F8 and A1 around 3 impacts; time from the last set-up motion to impact.
questions.challenge: If the video has no impacts, answer not determinable.
